Monument Square 8. bounded by Eliot Street, South Street, Greenough Avenue, Story Place, and along an imaginary line to South Street, Centre Street, Holbrook Street, Dane Street. This square been surveyed for its historic value and the specific houses on it have been evaluated. Each, in turn, will be described below, and the basis for its eligibility listed.
The square, and buildings surrounding it are the historic center of Jamaica Plain. One house in the area, the Loring-Greenough House, is on the N.R.H.P. The area contains plentiful examples of notable 19th century houses, inclding Gothic Revival, Italianate and Mansard houses; the neighborhood also has many Queen Anne, Shingle and Colonial Revival homes. The area has been studied by Dr. Cynthia Zaitzevsky, under contract to the Boston Redevelopment Agency, and a formal recommendation for its inclusion in the National Register has been made. Application is pending approval and action by the Boston Landmarks Commission and the Massachusetts Historical Society.
